Why do sexually reproducing organisms show more variation?
questions.a: Meiosis shuffles genes and fertilisation mixes genes of two parents, so offspring differ; asexual reproduction copies DNA almost exactly.

questions.q: What is the significance of variation for a species?
questions.a: Variations help populations survive drastic changes - some individuals may tolerate heat, drought or new disease.

questions.q: How are variations created during DNA copying?
questions.a: Copying is not perfectly accurate; small errors add up each generation, and in sexual reproduction new combinations arise.

concepts.title: Mechanism of Gene Expression and Chromosomes

questions.q: What is a gene made of and where does it sit?
questions.a: A segment of DNA sitting on a chromosome inside the cell nucleus.

questions.q: How does a gene control a trait like plant height?
questions.a: It guides making of a protein/enzyme; a less efficient enzyme makes less plant hormone, so the plant stays dwarf.

questions.q: What carries the information from parents to children?
questions.a: Chromosomes made of DNA in the gametes carry inherited information.
